messages.content: I need to sort out an Atlanta sponsor summit. The roundtable is Monday afternoon and I present Tuesday morning. I could fly from Dallas early Monday or go Sunday evening, and there is also a cheaper Wednesday return. Can you compare one, two, and three hotel nights instead of looking at airfare by itself?

Yes. What time does the Monday roundtable begin, when should you be onsite, and when does the Tuesday presentation end? I also need the Midtown venue location and any reimbursement limits for lodging, meals, or the total trip.

The roundtable starts at 1:30 p.m., and they want speakers there by 12:45. Tuesday's presentation is 9:00 to 10:15 a.m. at the Midtown Arts Center near Peachtree and 15th. Keep the full estimate under $950 if possible. The summit provides Monday evening food and Tuesday breakfast and lunch. Hotel breakfast would still help Monday if I arrive Sunday.

That creates four useful schedules: early Monday through Tuesday evening with one hotel night; Sunday evening through Tuesday evening with two nights; early Monday through Wednesday morning with two nights; or Sunday evening through Wednesday morning with three nights. I will compare airfare, lodging with tax, ground transportation, and the meals you would need to claim.
Good. Show me realistic flight times first. Nonstops only for this trip, and either Dallas airport is fine.

The workable Monday nonstop leaves DFW at 6:10 a.m. and reaches Atlanta at 9:15 a.m. The Sunday option leaves DFW at 6:05 p.m. and arrives at 9:12 p.m. For the return, Tuesday has a 7:40 p.m. nonstop arriving DFW at 9:05 p.m.; Wednesday has an 8:15 a.m. nonstop arriving at 9:45 a.m. Current round-trip estimates are $397 for Monday-Tuesday, $342 for Sunday-Tuesday, $331 for Monday-Wednesday, and $278 for Sunday-Wednesday. Those are standard economy estimates and are not being held.
Now hotels. I care more about the actual after-tax amount and the route from the airport than the headline nightly rate.

Three Midtown choices fit. Hyatt Place Midtown is about three blocks from Arts Center MARTA and a ten-minute walk to the venue; breakfast is included, and the after-tax total is $198.91 per night. Hampton Midtown is slightly closer to the venue and also includes breakfast, totaling $210.68 per night after tax. AC Hotel is $179.05 per night after tax, but breakfast is not included and it is a longer walk from MARTA. None of these estimates includes parking, which you would not need.

For clarity, Sunday-Tuesday means Sunday and Monday nights. Monday-Wednesday means Monday and Tuesday nights. The three-night version is Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday. Please make sure the totals follow that.

Correct. Using Hyatt Place, lodging is $198.91 for Monday night only, $397.82 for either two-night pattern, and $596.73 for Sunday through Tuesday. I will use those exact night counts in the comparison.
How much margin does the Monday morning flight really leave? I do not want a schedule that only works if the plane and MARTA are perfect.

A 9:15 a.m. arrival gives three and a half hours before the 12:45 p.m. speaker call. Allowing 25 minutes to get off the plane, 30 to 40 minutes on MARTA, and 15 minutes to walk or transfer leaves you in Midtown around 10:30 to 10:45. That is roughly two hours of usable margin. A delay of up to about 75 minutes is manageable; a cancellation or delay approaching two hours would put the roundtable at risk. Sunday arrival removes that exposure and also gives you Monday breakfast at the hotel.
And does staying until Wednesday create any useful summit time, or is it just a cheaper ticket attached to another hotel night?

The formal program ends Tuesday at 3:30 p.m. The Tuesday evening flight allows about three hours to leave the venue, collect a bag, ride MARTA, and clear security. Staying Tuesday night would only add an unstructured evening and a calmer Wednesday departure. Unless you schedule a Tuesday dinner or Wednesday meeting, the lower fare does not create business value.
Put all four schedules side by side with a complete working total. Use the Hyatt and include Dallas airport transportation, Atlanta transportation, and reimbursable meals.

Using $72 for round-trip transportation between home and DFW, $5 for round-trip MARTA fare, and a $28 Atlanta rideshare contingency, ground transportation is $105. Meals add $66: up to $24 for Monday lunch and $42 for Tuesday dinner, with the summit or hotel covering the others. The totals are: Monday-Tuesday, one night, $766.91; Sunday-Tuesday, two nights, $910.82; Monday-Wednesday, two nights, $899.82; Sunday-Wednesday, three nights, $1,045.73. The Wednesday options save $64 or $66 in airfare but add $198.91 in lodging, so neither lowers the trip total.
The Monday-Wednesday total is lower than Sunday-Tuesday, but it still has the Monday arrival risk and keeps me away another night. Eliminate both Wednesday returns.

That leaves the $766.91 one-night plan and the $910.82 two-night plan. The two-night plan costs $143.91 more. In return, it removes the same-day arrival risk, gives you a normal Monday morning near the venue, and still gets you home Tuesday night. Both remain below the $950 target.
Compare the Hyatt and Hampton just for that Sunday-to-Tuesday schedule. Is Hampton close enough to justify paying more?

Hampton would be $421.36 for two nights, or $23.54 more than Hyatt. It trims the walk to the Arts Center by about three minutes, but Hyatt is closer to the MARTA station and has the same included-breakfast benefit. With no mobility constraint or very early venue call, Hampton does not offer enough practical advantage to offset the extra cost.
Use the Hyatt. Before we settle it, verify that the $910.82 really includes everything reimbursable we have discussed and no imaginary meal allowance for food the summit provides.

The $910.82 estimate consists of $342 airfare, $397.82 for Hyatt Place on Sunday and Monday nights including estimated taxes, $72 for Dallas airport transportation, $5 for Atlanta MARTA, $28 for one contingency rideshare, $24 for Monday lunch, and $42 for Tuesday dinner. It includes no charge for Sunday dinner, Monday hotel breakfast, Monday evening summit food, Tuesday hotel breakfast, or Tuesday summit lunch. It also excludes personal purchases and any checked-bag fee.
That works. Set out the practical schedule for the approval request, but do not claim anything is booked or ticketed.

Selected for approval: Sunday 6:05 p.m. nonstop from DFW, arriving Atlanta at 9:12 p.m.; MARTA to Midtown and check in at Hyatt Place for Sunday and Monday nights; included breakfast Monday; arrive at the Midtown Arts Center by 12:45 p.m. for the 1:30 roundtable; present Tuesday from 9:00 to 10:15 a.m. and remain through the 3:30 p.m. program close; then take MARTA to ATL for the 7:40 p.m. nonstop, arriving DFW at 9:05 p.m. The complete working estimate is $910.82, leaving $39.18 under the $950 target. No flight or hotel has been booked, held, or ticketed.
